units.source_text: 南厅的大女公子入宫之后，大纳言邸内忽然冷清了。

en.t: After the eldest young lady of the southern quarters entered the palace, the Dainagon's residence suddenly grew quiet.

units.source_text: 尤其是西厅的二女公子，一向和姐姐常在一起，现在觉得非常寂寞。

en.t: The second young lady of the western quarters, who had always been with her elder sister, felt especially lonely now.

units.source_text: 东厅的女公子，即真木柱前夫所生的女公子，和这两位女公子也很亲昵。

en.t: The young lady of the eastern quarters, Makibashira's daughter by her former husband, was also very close to these two young ladies.

units.source_text: 晚上三人常常睡在一起，共同学习种种艺事。

en.t: At night the three often slept together and studied many kinds of arts together.

units.source_text: 关于吹弹歌舞等事，两女公子都向东厅女公子学习，当她师傅一般。

en.t: In matters such as wind and string music, singing, and dance, the two young ladies learned from the eastern young lady and treated her almost like a teacher.

units.source_text: 这位东厅女公子生性异常怕羞，对母亲也难得正面相看，其腼腆实在可笑。

en.t: This young lady of the eastern quarters was by nature extraordinarily shy, and she could scarcely look even her mother in the face, so that her timidity was almost amusing.

units.source_text: 然而品貌并不比人逊色，其娇媚之相远胜于他人。

en.t: Yet in character and appearance she was inferior to no one, and her charming grace far surpassed that of others.

units.source_text: 红梅大纳言想道：“我安排这个入宫，那个出嫁，只管为自己的女儿奔忙，实在对不起这位女公子。”

en.t: The Red Plum Dainagon thought that he had been busy arranging one daughter's entry into court and another's marriage, caring only for his own daughters, and that he had truly wronged this young lady.

units.source_text: 便对她母亲真木柱说：“这女孩子的婚事，你倘有了定见，快告诉我。

en.t: So he said to her mother Makibashira that if she had any settled idea about the girl's marriage, she should tell him at once.

units.source_text: 我一定同我自己的女儿一样看待她。”

en.t: He would certainly treat her just as he treated his own daughters.

units.source_text: 真木柱答道：“这种事情，我想也不曾想过。

en.t: Makibashira answered that she had never even thought about such a thing.

units.source_text: 勉强成就，反而对她不起。

en.t: If they forced a match, it would instead be doing the girl a wrong.

units.source_text: 只有听凭她的命运了。

en.t: They could only leave it to her fate.

units.source_text: 我在世期间，一定会照顾她。

en.t: As long as Makibashira was alive, she would certainly look after her.

units.source_text: 只是我倘死了，她很可怜，倒叫我担心了。

en.t: But if Makibashira died, the girl would be pitiable, and that was what worried her.

units.source_text: 然而那时她可出家为尼，就不致惹人耻笑，而自可安度一生了。”

en.t: Still, at that time she could take vows as a nun, avoid becoming an object of ridicule, and pass her life in peace.

units.source_text: 说罢流下泪来。

en.t: After saying this, she shed tears.

units.source_text: 又谈到这女公子性情之贤淑。

en.t: She also spoke of how virtuous and gentle the young lady's nature was.

units.source_text: 红梅大纳言对这三个女儿一样亲爱，毫无厚薄。

en.t: The Red Plum Dainagon loved these three daughters equally and showed no favoritism at all.

units.source_text: 但至今不曾见过这东厅女公子，颇思看看她的相貌。

en.t: But he had never yet seen the young lady of the eastern quarters, and he very much wished to see what she looked like.

units.source_text: 他常怨恨：“她只管躲避我，太没意思了。”

en.t: He often complained that she only kept avoiding him, which was terribly disappointing.

units.source_text: 想乘人不备时偷觑，或许可以看见一面。

en.t: He thought that if he stole a glance when no one was prepared, he might perhaps see her once.

units.source_text: 岂知连侧影也看不到。

en.t: Yet he could not see even her profile.

units.source_text: 有一次他坐在女公子帘外，对她说道：“你母亲不在家时，我应该代她来照顾你。

en.t: Once he sat outside the young lady's blinds and told her that when her mother was away, he ought to look after her in her place.

units.source_text: 你对我如此疏远，我很不高兴呢。”

en.t: He said he was very displeased that she kept such a distance from him.

units.source_text: 女公子在帘内约略回答数语，那声音文雅而婉转，可以想见其相貌一定也很美丽，是个很可怜爱的女子。

en.t: From behind the blinds, the young lady answered briefly; her voice was refined and gentle, suggesting that her face too must surely be beautiful, and that she was a very endearing girl.

units.source_text: 他一向确信自己的女儿优于别人，常以此自傲。

en.t: He had always firmly believed that his own daughters were superior to others and had often prided himself on it.

units.source_text: 此时他想：“我那两个恐怕赶不上这个人吧？

en.t: At this moment he wondered whether his two daughters might not be able to match this girl.

units.source_text: 如此看来，世界太大，也很讨厌。

en.t: Seen this way, the world was far too large, and that too was vexing.

units.source_text: 我以为我那两个女儿是出类拔萃的了，岂知世间自有比她们更强的人。”

en.t: He had thought his two daughters were outstanding, only to discover that there were people in the world who surpassed them.

units.source_text: 他越发渴慕这一位了，便对她说：“近几月来，不知怎的非常烦忙，丝弦也好久不听了。

en.t: He became still more drawn to this young lady and told her that for the past few months he had somehow been extremely busy and had not heard string music for a long time.

units.source_text: 西厅里你二姐正在用心学琵琶，大概她想精通此道吧。

en.t: In the western quarters, her second elder sister was studying the biwa earnestly, probably wanting to master that art.

units.source_text: 但琵琶这种乐器，学得似通非通，声音实在难听。

en.t: But with an instrument like the biwa, if one learns it only halfway, the sound is truly unpleasant to hear.

units.source_text: 如果可教，希望你悉心教导她。

en.t: If she could teach her, he hoped she would guide her with care.

units.source_text: 我并不曾专修某种乐器，但在昔年全盛之世，常得参与管弦之会。

en.t: He had never specialized in any particular instrument, but in the flourishing days of the past he had often taken part in concerts of wind and string music.

units.source_text: 全靠如此，对于无论何种乐器的表演，我都能辨别其手法之优劣。

en.t: Because of that, he could judge the quality of the technique in performances on any instrument.

units.source_text: 你虽然不曾公开表演过，但我每次听到你的琵琶之音，总觉得和昔年相似。

en.t: Although she had never performed publicly, whenever he heard the sound of her biwa, it always seemed to him like the music of former days.

units.source_text: 承受已故六条院大人真传的，现今世间只有夕雾右大臣一人。

en.t: In the present world, only Yugiri, the Minister of the Right, had inherited the true transmission of the late Lord Rokujo.

units.source_text: 源中纳言和匂兵部卿亲王，对无论何事都不让古人，真乃得天独厚之人。

en.t: Gen Chūnagon and Prince Niou, the Hyōbu Lord, were people blessed by heaven, inferior to the ancients in nothing.

units.source_text: 二人对音乐尤为热心。

en.t: The two of them were especially devoted to music.

units.source_text: 然而拨音的手法略嫌柔弱，毕竟赶不上右大臣。

en.t: Yet their plucking technique sounded somewhat too soft, and in the end they could not match the Minister of the Right.

units.source_text: 只有你的琵琶，手法和他非常相似。

en.t: Only her biwa technique was extremely similar to his.

units.source_text: 琵琶一道，按弦的左手必须熟练，方为佳妙。

en.t: In the art of the biwa, the left hand that presses the strings must be skilled before the playing can be truly fine.

units.source_text: 女子按弦时，拨音之声不同，带有娇媚之感，反而富有趣味。

en.t: When a woman presses the strings, the plucked sound is different, carrying a graceful charm that makes it all the more interesting.

units.source_text: 来，你来弹一曲吧。

en.t: Come, she should play one piece for him.

units.source_text: 侍女们！拿琵琶来！”

en.t: He called to the attendants to bring the biwa.

units.source_text: 侍女们大都不回避他，只有几个年纪最轻而出身较高的人，不肯被他看见，一味退入内室。

en.t: Most of the attendants did not avoid him, but a few of the youngest and highest-born refused to be seen by him and simply withdrew into the inner rooms.

units.source_text: 红梅大纳言说：“连侍女也疏远我了，真没趣啊！”

en.t: The Red Plum Dainagon said that even the attendants were keeping their distance from him, which was truly no fun.

units.source_text: 他生气了。

en.t: He became angry.
